basis: Defined by neurodevelopmental impairment, epilepsy, ataxia and other central nervous system manifestations.
Multiple congenital joint contractures and deafness define the syndrome; inguinal hernias add no distinct organ axis.
Definition localizes inflammation and fissuring to skin at the mouth corners; infection is not required.
Skeletal dysplasia with immunodeficiency (2/2); developmental delay/Chiari malformation and asthma each 2/2. Eczema (2/2) and cardiac defects (1/2) omitted at cap.
Congenital bladder dysfunction with vesicoureteral reflux (4/5). Constipation (3/5) alone does not establish direct bowel damage.
Tick-borne viral infection involving erythroid precursors and red cells, with leukopenia; encephalitis is uncommon despite the parent classification.
Alobar forebrain malformation; hypothalamic-pituitary dysfunction, especially diabetes insipidus, affects roughly 50-70% of severe HPE. Damaging eye defects vary.
Malignant epithelial tumour originating in the kidney; other manifestations of familial cancer syndromes are separate conditions.
Adenocarcinoma originating in minor salivary glands, which belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Defined by impaired binocular visual function.
Inherited corneal ectasia causing impaired vision.
Red-cell aplasia with defining mandibulofacial dysostosis; conductive hearing impairment and cleft palate each reported in 2/2 patients.
Childhood basal ganglia degeneration with dystonia and motor regression; hypotonia and elevated CK alone do not establish primary muscle disease.
Corynebacterium diphtheriae infection of the larynx; myocarditis and neuropathy are minority complications.
Acute bacterial infection and inflammation of the lacrimal sac.
Acrodynia is defined by acral dermatitis, mercury-induced peripheral/autonomic neurotoxicity and hypertension; frequency of destructive oral involvement is uncertain.
Squamous cell carcinoma originating in the larynx, part of the respiratory tract.
Malignant cartilage-producing tumour of bone or musculoskeletal soft tissue.
Purine-metabolism disorder; the supplied syndrome synonym identifies deafness and neurologic ataxia as defining manifestations.
Defined by cerebellar ataxia, developmental delay or severe epileptic encephalopathy.
COFS is defined by cerebral abnormalities, microphthalmia and skeletal abnormalities/contractures; supplied phenotypes confirm all three axes.
Congenital ichthyosis with impaired sweating; ectropion occurs in 2/11 patients, below the involvement threshold.
Umbrella of inherited cerebellar disorders; deafness, anemia and metabolic abnormalities are restricted to particular subtypes.
Congenital ocular malformations with visual loss; global developmental delay reported in 1/1 assessed patient supports neurologic involvement, with limited sampling.
Direct toxic injury to multiple peripheral nerves; the concept does not imply injury to other organs.
